It has also been stated that the petitioner was arrested from his residence on the night following 07-3-2007 in connection with Gulshan Police Station Case No.34(03) 2007 dated 26-10-2009 and he was duly produced before the Court and because of his serious illness the Government released him on parole and he went to London, UK for treatment at the Mall, South Gate, London. 

 11. Mr. Rafique-ul-Huq, the learned Senior Advocate along with Mr. Ahsanul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that this Court committed an error on the face of the record in not considering that the investigation of the instant case having commenced on 08-11-2009 as revealed in the charge sheet the alleged offence under the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain of 2002 in the instant case cannot be saved under Sections 6(b ), (c), (d) and (e) of the General Clauses Act, 1897 as none of the Sub- Sections of the said Section 6 attracts the instant case and as such, the judgment and order dated 09- 2-2011 may be reviewed by this Division. The learned Advocate for the petitioner then submits that this Court committed an error apparent on the face of the record in overlooking the aspect that the Ordinance Nos.VII, VIII and XVII of 2007 having embraced their natural death with effect from 25-2-2009, the Ain of 2002 has been deleted from the schedules of the said Ain of 2004 and the said Act of 1958 from 25-2-2009 and therefore, the said case having been instituted after 25-2-2009 from which date the said Ain of 2002 is no more subsisting in the schedules of the said Ain of 2004 and the Act of 1958, the Anti Corruption Commission cannot lodge the FIR, inasmuch as, the procedure of the said Ain of 2004 and the said Ain of 1958 cannot govern the proceeding of the instant case under the said Ain of 2002 and therefore, the said judgment and order dated 09-2-2011 may be reviewed by this Division. He finally submits that this Court committed an error apparent on the face of the record in holding that there is no bar to trial of the petitioner under provisions of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 (Act of 2004) for the commission of the offence alleged to have been committed under the Ain of 2002 and the question of prejudice does not arise because no tria can be held under the provisions of the Act of 2004, since Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 ceased to be an offence under the schedule of the Act of 2004 as well as Act of 1958 with effect from 25-2-2009 and that the Commission was not empowered to lodge the FIR under the Ain of 2002 and therefore, there is no scope to treat the instant case to be instituted under the Ain of 2002, which prescribes a different procedure for filing a money laundering case and also prescribes the person competent to file the case and as such, the judgment and order dated 09-2-2011 may be reviewed by this Hon'ble Division. 

 12. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney General appearing for the respondent No. 1 Government of Bangladesh submits that there is no merit in the submissions advanced on behalf of the petitioner since the petitioner has raised those points at the time of hearing of the civil petition for leave to appeal which are nothing but repetition of the selfsame points of law and fact and that .there is no legal ground to review the impugned judgment and order passed by this Division and as such the review petition is liable to be dismissed. The learned Attorney General then submits that the learned Advocate for the petitioner has failed to take notice that subsequent to the Ordinance Nos.VII and VIII of 2007 another Ordinance namely, the Ordinance No. XVII of 2007 was promulgated and by that Ordinance a new section, namely, Section 3(Ka) has been inserted in the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 and by that insertion of section 3(Ka) the Anti-Corruption Commission was given power to enquire into and conduct investigation of offences and to proceed in respect of an offence committed under the Money Laundering Protirodh Ain, 2002 and that the said Ain of 2002 was repealed by the Money Laundering Ordinance,2008 keeping the similar provisions of Section 3(Ka) in Section 9 of the Ordinance,2008 and Section 9 of the Ain of 2009. 

 19. Further the expression "error in the face of the record" has also been eloquently discussed by the Indian Supreme Court in the case of Thungabhadra Industries Lid. vs Government of Andhra Pradesh reported in AIR 1964 SC 1372 in the following terms: 

 23. In view of the aforesaid discussions and in the light of Article 105 read with Order XXVI of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh (Appellate Division) Rules, 1988 and the case laws discussed above, one may conclude that in order to review a judgment there must be an error apparent on the face of the record and that this error is so apparent and manifest and clear that no court of law would permit such an error to remain on the record. We are therefore convinced to reach to the conclusion that the error must not only be apparent but must also have a material bearing on the face of the case. In the case of LI.- Col. Nawabzada Muhammad Amir Khan vs Controller of Estate Duty, Government of Pakistan. Karachi reported in PLD 1962 SC 335 = 13 DLR (SC) 105 the Supreme Court of Pakistan observed as under: 

 32. In the impugned judgment passed in the Civil Petition we have observed that nowhere from the repealing Ordinance of 2008 or the subsequent Ain of 2009, one can find any indication stating the intention that repealing Act shows any different intention that such repeal has destroyed the liability or penalty incurred or investigation initiated under the repealed Ain of 2002. However, we have no hesitation in holding that the repealing Ordinance of 2008 or the Ain of 2009 has not destroyed the offence committed under the Ain of 2002. We are of the view that a prima facie case as has been dis- closed under the Ain of 2002 is found to have been saved by the provisions of Section 6(b), (c) and (e) of the General Clauses Act, 1897. It is well established that a criminal offence never abates or destroyed even after the repeal of the law under which the offence is alleged to have been committed. Section 6 of the General Clauses Act is applicable to a repeal of a law without any fresh enactment on the self-same subject and it is also equally applicable to a case of repeal of a law followed by fresh legislation in the same subject unless a different intention appears in the repealing law with that of the provisions of the Section and such different intention has to be ascertained from consideration of all the relevant provisions of the repealing law. In the impugned judgment it has been answered that inspite of repeal of the Ain of 2002 under which the offence was alleged to have been committed from 01-1-2003 to 31-5-2007, Section 6(b), (c) and (e) of the General Clauses Act enables the prosecution to continue with the legal proceeding or to institute any legal proceeding or to take recourse to any remedy which might have been effective before the repeal of the Act for getting remedy in respect of rights privilege, liability, penalty or punishment as the case may be. In that view of the matter in the impugned judgment we have held that the proceeding against the accused-petitioner may continue under the provisions of the Ain of 2002 as if the same Ain had not been repealed by the subsequent legislation. We have also observed that the procedure in respect of inquiry, investigation, conducting prosecution and holding of trial shall be governed under the provisions of the ACC Act, 2004 in view of the insertion of the Ain of 2002 in the schedule to the Anti- Corruption Corn mission Act, 2004. Furthermore by amending the Ain of 2002 a new Section namely. Section 3(ka) has been inserted in the Ain by Section 2 of the Ordinance No.17 of 2007. Section 3(ka) of the Ain of 2002 provides that the offences under the Ain of 2002 shall be treated as scheduled offences under the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 which shall be investigated by Anti- Corruption Commission and the said offences being the scheduled offences having been included in the schedule to the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 shall be triable by the Special Judge. Accordingly, inquiry, investigation, lodging of complaint and conduct of prosecution of cases and holding of trial in respect of those cases under the Ain of 2002 shall proceed under the Provisions of ACC Act, 2004 and that in case of any conflict with the provisions of the Ain of 2002, the provision of the ACC Act, 2004 and the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 shall prevail though the Ain of 2002 was repealed by the Ordinance of 2008 keeping similar provisions as of Section 3(ka) in Section 9 of the Ordinance of 2008 and also in Section 9 of the Ain of 2009.
